utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I begin this morning's proceedings with the Chamber's ruling on the submission that Prosecution witnesses should not be allowed to make an in-court identification of the accused Sikirica. This submission was based on Articles 20(1), 21(2) as well as Rules 89 A to D and 95. These provisions guarantee the accused the right to fair trial and, while allowing a Chamber to admit any evidence of probative value, they also empower a Chamber to exclude evidence if its probative value is substantially outweighed by the need to ensure a fair trial. They also require the exclusion of the admission of evidence which is obtained by methods that cast doubt on its reliability or if its submission would seriously damage the integrity of the proceedings. The essence of the submission is that it would be unfair to allow in-court identification of the accused since it was inevitable that a witness who had not identified the accused before the trial would pick him out in court. We were referred to the unfavourable view that common law courts took of in-court identification and to other methods of identification, such as a photo spread, that were open to the Prosecution. The Prosecutor, on the other hand, argued that it would be wrong to adopt a decision that would bar the admission of evidence of all witnesses who identified the accused in court. Rather, the Prosecutor argued that the evidence of each witness should be considered on its own merits. The Prosecutor also advanced arguments as to why, in the circumstances of this case, in-court identification should be allowed. However, in light of the view that the Chamber takes as to how this matter should be disposed of, it is not necessary to outline those arguments. The Chamber holds that it would be wrong to make a decision whose effect would be to exclude evidence of all witnesses which identify the accused in court. The Chamber will consider the admission of such evidence on an individual basis, and in arriving at its decision, will take into account the provisions of the Statute including Articles 20, 21, as well as Rules 89 and 95, and all the relevant factors such as whether the witness knew the accused prior to the camp incidents and the length of time which the witness spent in the camp along with the accused, Sikirica. That's the ruling. Would you now bring in the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ryneveld, the Chamber -- [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone to the Judge, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's also our intention to -- usually the first few witnesses, there are more details, even cross-examination takes longer. As people start to become more familiar with things, fewer details are asked, and so I anticipate that the proceedings will speed up. I've also mentioned to my friend, Mr. Greaves, that I do intend to perhaps do some more leading until stopped.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, and I encourage Defence counsel to examine the summary, witness summaries which are produced and identify beforehand those areas where leading can take place.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Before I proceed with this witness, do I understand that booklets of photographs have been distributed to the Court and to my learned friends?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No. No, we don't have any booklets of photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, might I ask you to take this set of photographs, please, and put them on the ELMO one by one. First of all, Your Honour, I have a booklet of photographs which we have tentatively marked as Exhibit 2. Our application will be to mark a bundle of photographs. There is some photographs marked 2A through -- the number appears to be I, and we're going to have the witness go through these photographs and outline where the rooms are and where various items are at the beginning so that the Court has an understanding, at least in terms of photographs, of what the terms of the balance of the witnesses will be talking about. Now, rather than have the booklet marked -- the booklet should be marked, but I've asked the usher to show the individual photographs on the ELMO so that the witness can use the pointer -- is there a pointer there -- to describe certain things for us.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Ryneveld: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: First of all, witness, I understand, sir, that you were placed in Room 1; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We were first taken to Room number 2. That is when we first arrived at Keraterm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, you told us about that yesterday, that you were in Room 2, and then after about 11 or 12 days, they moved you into Room 1. That's where we left off yesterday. Remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I believe you also told us yesterday that Room 1 was a little bit smaller than Room 2; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that it was about the same size as this courtroom, generally, roughly speaking?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, do I understand that at some point while you were there, there were about 300 to 350 men in that room at any one time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And, sir, I understand as well that you had to sleep on the concrete floor for the first nearly a month or so; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any blankets or bedding?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And eventually, were you given some wooden pallets to sleep on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like you to look at the photograph now marked on the ELMO beside you to the left. Do you recognize the building and the area depicted in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the Keraterm building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that the Keraterm building where you were brought along with your brother [redacted] on the buses on the 31st of May, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, recognising that this photograph was not taken on the 31st of May, 1992 but appears to be taken in February of 1996, what can you tell us about the way that the building looks in the photograph as compared to the way it looked when you were taken there in May of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right. What is missing was a small hut which was located just next to the traffic sign and where the guards were, and Sikirica was there also. There was a weigh -- there were scales there with -- protected by chains, and that is also missing as well as the hut.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. We will get to that in just one moment, sir. You see that there is a -- on the left side of the photograph, there seems to be a flat-roofed white building in front of the left side of the warehouse? Do you need glasses, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can see it now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that the weigh hut to which you are referring?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Perhaps, Mr. Usher, if you could put on photograph number 2 for a moment, I'll come back to -- that is photograph B -- photograph C, I'm sorry. Are you looking now at photograph 2C? Is that the hut and the chains that you're talking about, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And that hut is also shown on photograph 2A but it's just a little more difficult to see; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did notice it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's go back to the first photograph, 2A. Are you able to tell from that photograph -- can you describe for the Court, if you would, please, whether the rooms that you were taken to are shown on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you can see them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Going from left to right on the building - we will look at another - can you tell us where Room 1 was and where Room 2 was and where Room 3 was, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Room 1 was at the corner. Room number 2 was next to it, and then there was a door through which you entered to go to the kitchen and then the door to the toilet. Then Room number 3, Room number 4, and farther down, Room number 5, where they took people and beat them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. Now, still looking at photograph 2A, when the buses arrived at Keraterm that day - there is a gate at the front of the photograph - did you go through the gate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where did the buses stop?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: They would stop at -- near the dormitory number 2. There was a wider area there and we were put at -- against a wall. We were ordered to put our hands behind our back, to run along the wall, to turn around, to face the wall, to place our hands against the wall, and to spread our legs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, just so --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: With your permission, I can demonstrate how -- what we were ordered to do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. Just at the moment, I'd like to first of all find out where the buses were. Maybe we should take a different photograph. Perhaps you could show photograph 2B, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here is where the buses were parked, and we were over there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Room 1, is that shown in this photograph at the corner? You point out Room 1 for us with the marker.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Room 1 was here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And for the record, you're now pointing to the doorway on the left side of the photograph where the -- there appears to be a corner of the building; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Room 2 where you were first taken, where is that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was right next to it. That is where Room 2 was. And this is the door to Room 2, a somewhat smaller door than the door to Room 1, because this was a vehicle repair shop and this was a room. So the door was somewhat smaller.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the external layout of the building similar in 1992 than what we now see in these photographs? That means the outside.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: The outside view is the same.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, there seems to be an indentation where the building has -- comes out from the main building to the right of door 2; do you see what I'm talking about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is that -- where was Room 3?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Room 3 was here. There was a door leading to the toilet and then Room 3 was right next to it, and this was the door to it of Room 3.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You seem to be pointing with your pointer to a metal door that's just to the right of the lamp standard; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. Room 3 had a metal -- actually aluminum door.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And Room 4 was beyond Room 3, is that correct, going from left to right on the photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, except that the door -- the doors of Rooms 3 and 4 were quite far away from one another, and it was just a solid wall between the two of them, between Rooms 3 and 4 was the longest distance between any two doors so it should be somewhere around here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You can't see on the ELMO because the picture is not being shown. Now, sir, I'm going to ask you to quickly go through the remainder of these photographs for us and tell us if they look the way that you saw things back in May of 1992, in the summer of 1992. Photograph 2C you've already looked at. That is the close-up of the weigh hut just outside the Keraterm warehouse; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And we can see Rooms 1, 2 and 3 behind the weigh hut in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. This is 1, this is 2, and number 3.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And turning the page or going to the next photograph, to 2D, that is next another angle of the same weigh hut?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 2E, now that is a side view. We can see Keraterm on the left and on the right-hand corner we can just see the flat -- sort of in line with the mountains in the background, we can just see the flat roof of the corner of the weigh hut. Do you see that? Right on the extreme right-hand of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, is this the area where the buses parked, sir, when you arrived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the buses parked here. You cannot see dormitories number 2 and number 1. They are off the picture. The buses came to stop here. And here, on this side, there was an old truck that stood there parked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Shall we go to 2F. That is yet another photograph. Here again, we cannot see Rooms 1 and 2. We are starting to look at the, shall we say the extension of the building, is that correct? We are seeing Room 3 with a lamp standard.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. 2G. That's taken, I take it, from in front of the rooms looking back towards the weigh hut?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 2H, do you know what that area is in the foreground? Was that area there when you were there in 1992, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 2J, is that the perimeter fence around the camp? You can see the weigh hut on the right side and Keraterm facility in the background. Oh, that's in I, sorry, not J.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is the fence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much. Now, sir, let's go back to talking about what conditions were like when you were there. I understand, sir, that in Keraterm camp while you were there, there were about 1.350 people who had to share one toilet; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You'd be allowed to go to the toilet during the day most times except when there was a particular shift on duty; whose shift was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was Kole's shift which was one of the best shifts at the Keraterm camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there times when you were not allowed to go to the toilet?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Kole's shift we were never forbidden to go to the toilet, not once.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand, but my question was different. Was there a time when you were not permitted, in other words, disallowed from going to the toilet?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were periods during the Fustar's shift when we were not allowed to go out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how about at night? What sort of toilet facilities were available then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: At night, except in Kajin's and Kole's shifts when we could go out, during Fustar's shift we had to go to the toilet by using barrels and plastic bags.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there washing facilities for either yourselves or your clothes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There were some -- there was an opportunity during one of the shifts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do I understand, sir, that as a result of the conditions, the men and their clothes were basically filthy?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did people have lice?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's talk about food and water. For the first six days when you were there, did you get any food?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we were not given food, but when Kole's shift was on, he would ask if there was anything. He would say nothing. Sefik Brkic who was a salesman, said that there would probably be some food stocks, that is some milk or some other foodstuffs, in his -- in his store. Also Ibro Baktijarevic had some biscuits because he was a travelling salesman so he had some biscuits to hand out as presents when he travelled. Kole said that this would be good. He found a driver - I know who it was, it was Tomica - and they went and they brought this food to the camp and they distributed it out to the inmates.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ryneveld, I'm not clear as to what the witness said. He said, "When Kole's shift was on, he would ask if there was anything. He would say nothing." Could you just have him clarify that part?

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, as I understand your evidence, you weren't originally fed during the first six days, but once during Kole's shift, there was a question asked by someone of Kole or did Kole ask the prisoners about food, if there was anything available? Can you clarify that for us, please? Who did the asking?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I can explain it. Fustar's shift was on when we asked whether there was anything to eat, but he just cursed our mothers and he said, "Our own in Zenica are grazing grass in the stadium and you want something to eat." That was his answer. However, when Kole's shift came on duty, we also asked whether we could get something to eat. Kole said that there was nothing there, but the only thing would be if we could find some food, that he would allow someone to go there and get it. Then Sefik Brkic, the salesman --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us, and I understand they were allowed to go and they came back with milk and biscuits. Kole arranged for a driver to go with them and they came back with milk and biscuits which they shared among some of the prisoners, is that correct? And this is Room 1 prisoners or all the prisoners in all the rooms, 1350 of them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. Because in those days, there was only Room Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. number 2 because men from Puharska were the first ones who were captured and brought there. Fifteen days later they started to collect the men from Selci, Kozarac, Hambarine, Rizvanovici, so that there were more people. In Room 3, there was Karlovac Brewery shop, so they emptied that in order to house more inmates in it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but my question, sir, is when the milk and cookies or biscuits were brought back, was there enough to feed everyone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those who were there welcomed it. It was not enough for all of us, but we shared it among us as much as it was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: How many shared this food? That is the question.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were 350 to 400 men who shared that food.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, you've talked about one incident when you were allowed to go out and get the milk and cookies. How about during the balance of your stay, was there enough food for everyone and what was the food like? How often were you fed? Tell us about that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there wasn't enough food. Later on, after those biscuits and bread, the kitchen finally began to work. A truck would bring the foodstuffs. First at 7.00 bread would arrive. And if you would put the photograph here, I could show you where the bread was brought because it was brought and left near the WC, next to the wall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question, sir, is how often were you fed? Were you fed every day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once a day, once the kitchen started to work.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What would they feed you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hot water with a cabbage leaf or perhaps some pasta.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: First of all, the photograph number you're referring to --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here it is. This is where bread was unloaded every morning, and at 7.00 in the morning, and it would just stay there. It would be left there for about three or four hours on the concrete here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are now for the record referring to photograph 2B, at the area near the toilets where the indentation is between the toilets and the extension known as Room 3; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is right, here, and then comes the lavatory and Room number 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Your Honours, I note I have neglected to actually make an application to admit the bundle of photographs as an exhibit in these proceedings, and with your permission I would ask that they be marked as Exhibit 2, 2A through 2J.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this hot water you're talking about that sometimes had a cabbage leaf in it, was there ever any macaroni or pasta in there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. When there was cabbage, it was water with a leaf of cabbage, and when pasta, pasta. They were so few and far between in that water that you had to chase them in the plate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you would get a slice of bread, can you tell us what the bread looked like and why?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can. People didn't get one, they got two slices of bread, everybody, and you looked through it, you could see Kozarac, you could see the mountain through your slice of bread because the bread was machine sliced.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was it clean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so because it was left in front of the lavatory. It was covered with flies. You look at it, it's all black with flies because it arrives there at 7.00, half past 7.00, and it's in sun because there is little shade there, and they would be there for several hours sometimes, depending on when women who distributed the food to us would arrive.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to try to summarise some of this evidence for you. Is it fair to say that during your stay at Keraterm, which is approximately two months, that you lost 16 kilograms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that because you didn't have enough to eat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the eating process itself, were you given all the time you needed in order to eat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we did have enough time when Kajin and Kole's shift were on. Then we had enough time to eat decently. But when Fustar's shift was on, then Banovic would say, "You've got one minute to finish. Stop." That is we would be stopped the very same moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if you weren't finished, what would happen to your food?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was thrown away. That is I suppose they threw it away. And if you went on eating, you'd get a baseball bat on your back, so we simply had to quit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Sir, do you recall a prisoner by the name of Car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, after you arrived in the camp on the 31st of May, how long after you arrived did Car arrive, do you recall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was three or four days later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I understand, sir, that as a result of what you saw, this prisoner died; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: The prisoner did not die. The prisoner was killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean he did not die of natural causes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that. Perhaps you could describe for us what you saw at Keraterm camp that resulted in his death.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw Duca and Zigic. Duca had a baton with a metal ball on top of it. When he was brought to Keraterm, Zigic took up the heavy machine-gun to Car and ordered him to put it on his shoulders and run in a circle. And as he ran past, Duca would hit him with the baton on the head. This metal ball would hit him on the forehead. He -- blood would pour, and Zigic would hit him on his legs and say, "On your feet, Car, can you?" And Car would answer, "Yes, I can." "So get up." So it was repeated several times until Car remained lying down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what room this prisoner Car was in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was in Room 2. At that time prisoners were only in Room 2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was there an incident with a bottle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us about that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Duca and Zigic brought him to the room with prisoners and asked him, "Car, tell us three men you know and we won't beat you any more." And I think he must have known at least 70 per cent of all those people, but his answer was, "I don't know anyone." Zigic then went out, got a bottle, a mineral water bottle, a litre one, put it on the floor, ordered Car to take off his trousers and his underpants. And then when he did so, then he ordered Car to sit on that bottle and as Car squatted, he pushed him down. He pressed against his shoulders so as to press him on that bottle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And thereafter, did anything else happen to Car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: They beat him again. He fell, could not stand up any more, and then two prisoners were ordered to take him into the room, into Room 2, and not ten minutes later, Car died. The order came to take him out. I can show it -- I'll show you on the photograph where is it where he was lying. And that was the first time that I saw a physician in the camp called Jelenkov, a psychiatrist, who put on white thin gloves, looked at Car and stood above him for some five or six minutes, took off his gloves, and left the camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're now looking at some photographs again and perhaps you can tell us what the -- on the back, I think on the photographs is a number. I think you are showing us --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just let me see. Just a moment. This, I think, shows it best.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It looks like you're showing us number 2A, the first photograph, yes? You are pointing to where? Use your pointer, if you would.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm pointing at dormitory 1 and 2. There is some asphalt here, but there is some grass here next to the lamp post, and that is where Car was lying dying when Jelenkov examined him. And when he established his death, the order came to put him in a wheelbarrow, and that is what they did, and they took him away and just threw him over the garbage dump.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. If you could go to photograph 2E, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is the area shown on photograph 2E where he was first of all beaten and then where his body was dumped?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The place where he was beaten is not shown here. I'll show you that. But it was next to this lamp post, this corner here. That is where Car lay dead.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And for the record, you're pointing to the lamp standard that's in front and centre of the photograph, and this corner you're referring to is the left side of the photograph near the forefront. All right. Sir, how long --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: In front of it is the path which is almost, almost straight. And they beat him here in the compound, in the circle. You can't see it here, because he had to run in circles with that machine-gun, not the --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long was he forced to run in circles with the heavy machine-gun?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I should say not less than one hour. I'm sure not less than that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who are Duca and Zigic that you mentioned in your evidence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were Serb soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if they were part of someone's shift and, if so, whose shift were they on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think they were on anyone's shift. They were roving soldiers who went to Omarska to beat and to Keraterm, the same group, Janjic, Zigic, Duca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you happen to know any of their -- whether Duca, for example, that's a nickname, is it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think it is his nickname.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know his full name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: His full name, no, only Duca. That is how I remembered him --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were any --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- fat, big.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any other guards or soldiers involved in the beating of Car during the incident that you've just described for the Court?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Duca, Zigic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said earlier that he was being beaten. Who was doing the beating, just Duca and Zigic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only Duca and Zigic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I understand that after about two weeks or the 11 or 12 days you've told us that you went into -- from Room 2 into Room 1, but before that happened, you were interrogated; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do I understand that the interrogations took place upstairs in the same complex?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if we were to look at photograph 2A, we can see there are two floors.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would the interrogations take place upstairs above Room 1 there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's where you were interrogated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell us, sir, I'm going to just ask you, you understand that you knew the person who interrogated you; is that correct? He was a traffic policeman in Prijedor prior to the war.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were interrogated about 15 minutes and you were asked personal questions at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. He asked personal questions. He was quite a man with dark complexion who sat there, and I learned that he had arrived from Banja Luka but Kondic interrupted him. He shouted. Shouted obscenities saying, "You from Puharska don't know what is going on, but we shall use different methods of interrogation with you."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They didn't use any different methods with you, did they, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is -- that's right, they did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after about 15 minutes of this, you were then led back into Room 1 where, eventually, [redacted] [redacted] is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So is it fair to say that immediately after your interrogation, you were taken out of Room 2 and moved into Room 1?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was it Kajin's shift that was on at that particular time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know Kajin before the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us how it is that you knew Kajin before the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I would see him around the town. I was -- I knew his father very well. That's how it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he know you by sight or by name as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: He must have known my name, not my full name. He knew my nickname.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you told what your job was going to be?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. All he said [redacted] [redacted] He did not tell me that I had to do this or that. No, he did not say that, ever.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the communications with the prisoners in Room 1 thereafter go through [redacted], or how did that work?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you in fact keep track of how many people were in Room 1?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: To be quite honest, I did not. I told him, "Come, write down the names that you want to," and believe me, I had no contact with Kajin. I did not receive any information from him, nor did I give any information to him. Only when they needed somebody to work, they would say, "Give us two or three men." There were those guard chiefs and they would say, "Give us two or three men" because there were those four dormitories.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, did you recognise Kajin when you saw him when you were at the -- at Keraterm, when you arrived? Did you recognise this man right away as somebody you knew?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I saw him. I saw him not when we arrived, not just then, but when -- after we had been put in that room. I saw him from the room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you saw him from the room, did you know who he was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew it was Kajin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, I understand that there is a man by the name of Zejro Causevic. Do you know him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I understand, sir, that Zejro Causevic you knew to be a man who worked in a butcher shop that had been owned by a Serb. He was brought to Keraterm; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were already in Room 1 by then, when he arrived at the camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you recall an incident when a man that you earlier referred to as Tomica called him out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I understand, sir, that you saw him being beaten. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I did not see him being beaten. Tomica called him out, took him away, and as he came back, he was crawling on all fours as a dog, and Tomica shouted, "Come back." And he said, "Tomica, brother, kill me right here. Just not make me come back."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if I have it right, this man was called out of your room, and you didn't see what happened to him, but on the way back, he was crawling on all fours. Did you see anything about him that led you to believe that he'd been beaten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I came close to Zejro, he was all black, and he had cuts above his eyes. And when I looked at Zejro, he was all covered with wounds, so I said, "Zejro, what did they beat you with?" And he said, "Chains, cables and even a plank full of nails."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that the only incident, sir, involving beatings of Causevic by Tomica or did that happen again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: It happened twice. What I have just told you was the second time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And after the second time, sir, the gentleman came into -- back into your room; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zejro, you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, Zejro.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this after the second beating?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the second beating.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And to make a long story short, sir, I understand that he was having great difficulty from his injuries and he was -- he was running a high temperature, and eventually, I understand, sir, that you were trying to get some medical help for him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us about that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a shortage of water and he was thirsty all the time, so if somebody had any water, he gave it to him, but when we ran out of water, it was Fustar's shift so we tried to see who would go to bring some water, but nobody dared do that, and Zejro could not stand it any more so he picked up a bottle, urinated in it, and then drank his own urine. And Edin, who slept next to him -- and Edin Porcic said to me, "Listen, Zejro's got worms," and I came and I saw huge worms emerging from his wounds. So I went to Fustar and asked for a doctor to be brought in, and he promised that he'd get a doctor but a doctor did not come. After that, I went to Sikirica and I asked him about the doctor, and he said he'd see about the doctor, but he did not. So I went to Sikirica again and I asked to be allowed to take him out because there the sun was very strong so worms might get out by themselves and he allowed me to get him out. I can Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. show it to you on the photograph. I brought him out here on to the grass here in front of dormitory 1. And then as I looked, there was a barrel full of water, and when I looked, Zejro was drinking from it and washing his wounds. And then a soldier called Kondic turned up and drove him away from there and said, "Why don't you go back to dormitory?" And Zejro said, "Well, the room leader won't let me into the room." And I heard that fortunately, and I explained to the soldier that it was Sikirica who had ordered me to take the man out. So he did nothing, he merely kicked Zejro and said, "Get up and get back into the dormitory," and made him go into the dormitory again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the effect of all of this is that Sikirica did not arrange for a doctor either for Zejro; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did Zejro Causevic, did he leave the camp at some point? And how?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: A military truck arrived and they asked for 15 volunteers every day, and we room leaders had to give some from every room. So knowing what the Serb had told me, never volunteer for anything, so that from my room, from my dormitory, nobody except Zejro volunteered for anything. And that truck came ten times at least during ten days, that is once a day, and when they got 15 men, then Kondic told Zejro, "Zejro, up into the truck," and Zejro climbed into the truck and they drove him away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You never saw him again after that, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never. Either him or those other men who left in the truck. I never heard about them again, nor do their relatives know anything about them.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Excuse me one moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a question for clarification, sir. It may be that I misunderstood you. Did you say that when you were asking Sikirica for help and he was dealing with Zejro, did I hear you say that Sikirica kicked Zejro or did I mishear that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He did not kick Zejro.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: But when he had stripped and he was sitting down, this soldier named Kondic arrived and he kicked him and said, "Go back in the room."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that while Sikirica was around?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can guarantee -- I don't know if he was looking directly, if he was looking at it at that point. He could have seen it. But no, Sikirica was not around that time. Sikirica was only moving around this weigh hut.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, sir, you've told us about Sikirica. Did you know Sikirica before the conflict?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew him by sight slightly. I worked at the marketplace for a long time so it may be a week -- we knew each other from the marketplace or from the sports games, but when I saw his face it looked familiar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you learn Sikirica's name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you say that you went to sports games. Were those football games?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, football games, handball games, soccer. I liked sports.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And to your recollection, you think that you may have seen Sikirica at some of the football games and where you worked in the marketplace; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do I understand you correctly that the man looked familiar but you didn't know what his name was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you -- first of all, sir, how long were you in Keraterm? From the 31st of May until when?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until 2nd of August. Then they loaded us up and took us to Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So for the months of July and August you were at the camp and during that period of time -- sorry, the months of June and July?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: June and July, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And during that period of time, did you have many occasions to see the man who was identified to you by the name of Sikirica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see him often?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, almost every day, in the morning, 7.00, from 7.00 in the morning until about 4.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you describe the man that you understood to have the name of Sikirica for us now? Can you describe him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was well-built. He had a moustache. He was wearing camouflage uniform. He was about 170 to 175 centimetres tall, maybe slightly taller than I am. It was sort of darkish blond hair, not dark hair but darkish blond.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he have any weapons on him at any time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was carrying a pistol.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what can you tell us, from what you could see, about what position he held at Keraterm? Did you draw any conclusions about his position?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would often see him when he came in the morning. He would take a black bound notebook. He would cross over the compound to take it to the investigators. It was probably the list of detainees to be questioned. About ten minutes after that, they would start calling these names out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And how did he relate with the other guards or the other people like Kajin and Kole that you've referred to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say how he behaved towards them, whether he issued them orders or not. I would not be able to say anything about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you see about them, and the way in which they would deal with Mr. Sikirica? Can you relate to us some of the things that you saw them do that made you come to a conclusion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could conclude something like this: For instance, when the volunteers were needed when this truck would come and they -- when they were asking for volunteers first, it would start from Sikirica, 15 volunteers then commander would pass it down to us. He would say, "Give us three to four men from each room."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You used the word "commander". Who are you referring to when you use that word?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was referring to Sikirica, because the fact he was a commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then he would tell you the commander would say, "Give us three or four men," and before they said that, you'd see them talking to Sikirica. Is that a fair summary of how you've described that for us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the order approximately in which it went. Sikirica took Kole or Kajin and then they to us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, sir, this Sikirica that you saw over a period of some two months almost every day at the camp, some nine years have passed, but do you think that you would recognise this man today if you were to see him again today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, perhaps I could recognise him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ryneveld, we are coming to this matter that arose some controversy. Is there any dispute about this on the part of the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: We don't accept that the man he is about to identify is one and the same as the person he's identified as the commander or Sikirica. We don't accept that that's the same -- that the defendant is the same person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Witness A, help us with this: How long before the war had you known this man who you were told was Sikirica? For what period before the war had you known him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew him before the war perhaps five or six years prior to the war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We will allow the identification to take place.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you, sir, that if -- would you please look around the room, if you would, and in the event the person that you have been referring to as the Sikirica that you saw in the camp every day, if you see that person in the room today, would you please tell us if he is here, where he is, and perhaps what the person may be wearing. Would you look around now, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Sikirica is sitting there. He is wearing a beard. He has a tie, a suit. He is the second next to the security officer. He has a moustache and beard. That is Sikirica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you're now, for the record, looking at the wall to the -- to your left, to the right of Their Honours, and are you going from left to right when you say the second person beside the security guard? Is that from left to right as you are looking at the line of gentlemen against the wall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am looking at this side next to the security guard is -- next to him and on the other side is Kajin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Oh, I see. Kajin, this is a gentleman that you've indicated earlier to us as someone that you knew. You've identified Kajin as well.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So we have a security guard, then Sikirica, then Kajin and then another security guard?

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Objection. Your Honours, I wouldn't object if there was a foundation for this identification of my client.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I haven't got to Mr. Vucicevic's client.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, we're dealing with Sikirica.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: But in relation to exactly where he is sitting, the witness has indicated that he's between the security guard and a person he knows as Kajin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. It seems to us that he has already identified the accused Sikirica.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, you've told us earlier that some people would be taken to Omarska; is that correct? Did you ever see an incident where Mr. Sikirica would read out names before people were transported to Omarska?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In particular, I understand you had a brother who you've told us about, [redacted], who went into the room with you. Did he leave the camp at some point?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: My brother [redacted]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. How is it that he left the camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: My brother was taken for questioning about 15 minutes before I did. Then I was right next after him. When I entered, his file was there, and they were filling out the forms for questioning. And not knowing that this file was separated and that he was going to go to Omarska, it was 8.00, 8.30 in the morning, I couldn't quite say what time it was because we did not have watches. A police Land Rover arrived driven by Grahovac and eight or nine men went to Keraterm. [redacted], my sister's son went there, Daniel Ahmic, and a doorman who used to work at the Mir Cicota company. He lived close to where I lived, so eight or nine men in total went.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it was -- you've spoken to your brother since that incident, I take it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After your brother and these people were taken away, you have then, since being taken away, spoken to your brother?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we had no contact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In recent years have you had contact with your brother [redacted]?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: In recent years, after he was released from the camp, he was first taken to Omarska, then to Manjaca, and then to Karlovac. When I left my town, I went to Karlovac and this is where I was reunited with my brother.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. And you learned from your brother that after he left Keraterm, that he went to Omarska; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I learned it from my brother when we were reunited.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. All right. Now, you've told us earlier, I believe, that it was Mr. Sikirica who would take his black notebook and would go upstairs and then people would be called out for interrogation; is that correct? Is that what happened the day that you and your brother were called upstairs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, during your time at Keraterm, I understand you witnessed or saw or heard of a number of beatings taking place; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From your observation, what happened when new prisoners arrived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: New detainees would be brought out of vans or cars here by the weigh station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what would happen to them as they arrived at the camp on a regular basis.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: A search, removal of personal belongings, documents, et cetera, and then beating.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that an invariable routine, did that happen to just about all the new arrivals?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, all who arrived were searched and so on. I remember my late relative was forced to eat a small bank note. They were angry because they did not find more money with him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll get to that sir, but what I'm trying to establish is when prisoners arrived, they would be searched and beaten and that happened, what, during the daytime, or would they arrive at night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the most part they would arrive during daytime.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you've told us earlier, I believe, that Sikirica you would see on the day shifts; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What can you tell us, sir, as these prisoners arrive and were being searched and beaten, was that ever in Mr. Sikirica's presence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that he had to have been present.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you ever recall incidents where you saw him present?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because he was sitting inside the hut, and people who would -- who were bringing detainees would go to the hut. In fact, I can say that I never saw Sikirica hit anyone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you've told us, sir, that about between 10 or 15 times, I believe 10 times you told us today, that a military truck would come to the camp, and that they would want volunteers, and I believe you told us that you had been told by someone, by a Serb, never to volunteer. Can you tell me about what you could see about the way in which Mr. Sikirica would get involved, if at all, in the selection of volunteers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: First, Sikirica did not select people. Sikirica would only say, "I need 15 volunteers," when the truck would come. He would say this to the commanders, either to Kajin, to Fustar, to Kole. And then they would go immediately to the leaders of the rooms, and they would say three or four men from Room 1, from Room 2, from Room 3. Fortunately, no one went from my room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Except for Zejro.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I understand that. Now, were there other vehicles that arrived when people would volunteer to go on a different vehicle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was a blue TAM truck, 2001 model, and those men would come back to the camp every night. They were in good moods, and they were never hungry which means that they were given food.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what effect did the fact that when this blue truck took volunteers and these people came back not hungry, what effect did that have on people wanting to volunteer for those shifts?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what effect it had, what effect could have been. I really could not say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did people volunteer to go on the blue two-tonne truck?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, many wanted to, but only the first group who had volunteered initially was selected. So the same people went time and time again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. Do you know what they were volunteering to do? What was their task? Did you know what they were volunteering for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sure that they wanted to leave the conditions that we were in, to get some food, perhaps to see one of their own, because the conditions were really terrible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's move on if we could, please, to Mr. Karabegovic. Do you know Mr. Karabegovic or did you know Mr. Dzevad Karabegovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. [redacted].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, sir, I understand that about ten days after you were put in [redacted] Room 1, this individual, Mr. Karabegovic was brought to Keraterm; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I believe you've made reference to this just a few moments ago that he was searched and the guards found some money on him that you -- that was useless, and I think you've just told us that he was forced to put it in his mouth and eat the money; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see this happen or did he tell you about this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally saw this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see whether or not he was beaten at the time of his arrival?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was slapped once, and he was forced to eat up this bill. This was done by the soldiers who had brought him to Keraterm. This was not done by the guards there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I understand, sir, that after he was in your room for about a month, and he shared a pallet with you and some of your other fellow prisoners, that he was called out by Mr. Banovic, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. He was -- he called him out one night. This was around 11.00, 11.30. He said, "Dzevad Karabegovic." And he responded. When he came to the grate -- to the bars, he gave him a piece of bread, and a drumstick, chicken drumstick and a tomato. We were surprised, and we took it and we shared it among us. The next night around the same time, Banovic called him out. We thought that this was food and so we were elated, but in fact, he took him out, and this was again 11.30 at night. Around 12.00 - this wasn't very long, maybe half an hour - the door opened and something fell in. I went over to see, and the people who were sitting up front said that this was Dzevad. I got up. I took him in my arms, and I asked Suljo Crnkic, Said Hergic and Saim Balagic to make room for him so that he could lie down on the pallet. Then I felt something sticky on my hands. I asked the man next to me - that was Besim Ceric - I asked if I could have a lighter because I wanted to see what it was. He said, "Please don't light it because if they see that something is going on they may shoot." And I said that I had to do it. When I saw it, I was all covered in blood. He was wearing a blue sweater. When I pulled it up, I saw that his back was not blue but Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. black. I looked to see where the injury was, and when I pulled up to see on -- on his left arm, there was a deep gash on -- above the -- in the upper hand, and there was something like a tendon sticking out, and the blood was running like when you slaughter a chicken. I called a doctor. He came over and we said, "Do we have anything to use as a bandage?" I said, "I have a T-shirt. Can I use that?" He said that we could. Then I took it off, we tore it off, and we bandaged him. However, at around 1.30, he died.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I take it the next morning his body was taken away?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I asked detainees not to report this right away, that is not until the dawn, because some were saying, "You have to report that he's dead so that he can be taken out." But I asked for them to wait until the dawn. When I could not take him out, Saim Balagic took him. I took off his shoes and gave them to Suljo because he had none. So Suljo took him, carried him out, and Saim and Said. I followed them, crying, and Banovic saw me crying. I said -- he said, "Why?" I said, "I feel sorry for Dzevdo." He said, "What Dzevdo?" And I said, "Dzevdo Karabegovic, he died." And he said, "Well, that's a mistake." This is what he told me, "That's a mistake." He asked, "How long has he been there?" I said, "About a month." He said, "This is a mistake." I don't know if it was a mistake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Is there anything more on this incident? Because we are now at the time for the break. And also time for the witness to compose himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Yes. I understand. Thank you. I just have one more question but I'll do that after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. 11.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Greaves.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Your Honour, there is a very short matter I'd like to raise, please, before the witness comes back in. Your Honour, it relates to the identification that took place this morning, an observation that Your Honour made at 10.45 whilst we were discussing the matter. Your Honour said this: "It seems to us that he has already identified the accused Sikirica." I don't want to sound critical in any way, but it could sound to the defendant, in particular, that Your Honours have already made up your mind that it's a good identification. And what Your Honour may have meant to say was: His evidence is that he's identified Sikirica, and I'm concerned because I haven't yet cross-examined the witness on this issue of identity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, that's precisely the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I'm very grateful, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Your Honours, while the witness is being brought in, I am concerned about the length of time that this is taking, and although I realise it is the first witness and we've got to get into a -- I do intend to attempt to do some more leading, and I'm just giving everybody some notice that if I'm going to get through this hopefully in the next session, I probably am going to use the material here and try to stay away from areas that are really controversial but lead on the rest. That's -- unless Your Honours have some other instructions for me, I'm going to try and lead a little bit more unless my friends take strenuous --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I think you should adopt that procedure, because the counsel for the Defence do have your summary, and they are in a position to object, if they so wish, to leading. When you started, I did, myself, think that Defence counsel might have been a little more understanding and liberal in background matters. I believe you ought to be able to lead on background matters so that we can move more expeditiously. This is an important witness, however, and he does have a lot of evidence on important issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: And we're moving now into an area where there are, perhaps, issues involving the three accused that I can't lead on so that's -- anyway, I'm just letting you know that I'm concerned about the time that this is taking, and I am going to attempt to summarise some of the noncontroversial areas as best I can, and I undertake to not lead on areas that I think will be controversial.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vucicevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: I would agree what Your Honour said in leading on general matters. But when I reviewed the summary of the evidence that this witness is about to present, it just came to my mind that paragraphs 15 and 16 deal with the massacre and I believe that's highly controversial, and I would respectfully suggest that no leading takes place by introducing the evidence in those two paragraphs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: 15 and --

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: We've passed those.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We've done those already.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: We're about to do 21.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I think you are a little behind, Mr. Vucicevic. Yes, please call the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You meant 35 and 36.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Will the counsel switch on his microphone, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: I'm talking about the massacre, whatever paragraphs that is in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No doubt you will bring that to our attention.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness A, I understand you've already told us you were [redacted]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [redacted]?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall an incident where Kole called the four [redacted] [redacted]?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I understand, sir, that at that point, all the prisoners who were then in Room 3 were ordered to line up outside the room. Is that also correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, objection. This is leading here.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ryneveld?

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: This is to me an incident before the Room 3 incident that my friend is concerned about. This is the emptying of the room. However, if my friend -- we are going to spend more time dealing with objections than me trying to summarise it. Fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: My objection still stands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, sir, why were you called together?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were called to be -- then told to take into our rooms some men from Room 3 because Room 3 had to be emptied.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you told what was going to happen to the people that were in Room 3, where they were to go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: They said men from Room 3, we were to take some 50 into my room, some 50 into Room 4, and about 120 or thereabouts into Room 2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who told you to do this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was Kole who told us to do that. He called us all and said, "Please don't ask any questions. There are no any -- additional questions. Room 3 needs to be vacated."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand you didn't ask any further questions but were you given any reasons as to why Room 3 had to be emptied?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you take a number of prisoners into your room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By the time you did, can you give us an estimate about how many people you now had in Room 1?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Room 1, at that moment, there were about 350 people -- men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you remember approximately when it was during your detention at Keraterm that this emptying of Room 3 took place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: When? Around 11.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, months, dates, do you have any idea? I understand it was about 11.00. Was it in June or July or August or May or when? Or do you recall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Early July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, after the room was emptied, did some other prisoners arrive?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not immediately. They arrived in late afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know where these men were from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those men were from Hambarine, Rizvanovici, Rakovcani.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what kind of villages were those, ethnically speaking?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There was a question, sir, that I forgot to ask you earlier. What is your ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These people that arrived from these Muslim villages that you've just named, where were they put when they arrived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were first left on that grass next to the booth that was there, on the grass. And that is where they spent the night. And the next morning, they went into Room 3.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These villages that you've mentioned, sir, are those villages from the Brdo area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when these people arrived, I understood they arrived by bus, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember what happened to these prisoners? Perhaps I can be more specific. Was there an incident where an old man was required to perform a prayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Objection. Your Honour, I object to this question -- against this question. The question was was there an incident. It is up to the witness to say whether there was an incident and what kind of incident. That is without any leading as to the kind of incident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ryneveld?

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: I take my friend's point. I was trying to direct the witness to a particular incident. Otherwise, we could have any one of a number of incidents being recounted. However, I understand my friend's objection and he is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness A, did you see an incident on that particular day that you can tell us about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did. When they were brought there, there was an old man among them, and one of the soldiers -- there were very many troops who had brought them there, and one of the soldiers forced this old man to pray, to show how he prays to his God, and he was ill-treated and beaten, and then I heard a shot.
